# Results — Study 394 (Defense-Basket)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The folklore — **"defense
stocks reliably rally on war and rearmament headlines"** — tested as an **event study**.
We take a fixed, hardcoded set of **20 geopolitical-shock dates** (US strikes, invasions,
Russia–Ukraine, Israel–Iran…) and measure the equal-weight defense basket's cumulative
return **in excess of SPY** over the trading days after each shock, entering **one day after**
the headline (no look-ahead). Offline & deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted closes — **LMT, RTX, NOC, GD** (equal-weight defense basket), **ITA** (sector ETF, robustness), **SPY** (market). Public, no key. |
| Window | 1995-01-04 → 2026-06-18 (**7,917** trading days; **31.5** years) |
| Defense basket | equal-weight daily return of the four prime contractors; `excess = basket − SPY` |
| Shocks | **20** hardcoded war / invasion / rearmament headline dates (see [references](references.md)) |
| Event window | cumulative excess over **5 / 21 / 63** trading days after the shock |
| Entry / costs | 1-day execution lag; one all-in round-trip of 10 bps on the long-basket / short-SPY pair |

> **As-of: 2026-06-18** (last cached bar). The shock dates are chosen on the *headline*,
> ex-ante — never on the outcome. ITA only lists from 2006, so the four single names carry the
> long history and ITA is a shorter-window cross-check on its own.

## The signal — defense's excess-over-SPY return after a shock vs the base rate

1-day entry lag; the unconditional column is *all* overlapping forward windows over the same
tape (the honest base rate for the basket's drift relative to SPY). The plain *t* tests the
event-window excess against zero; the HAC *t* is Newey-West on the pooled in-window daily
excess; the placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random same-size date draws whose mean
event-window excess **beats** the shock set.

| window | n shocks | cond. mean | cond. win-rate | base mean | base win-rate | plain *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 20 | **−0.14%** | 45% | +0.08% | 52% | **−0.19** | −0.19 | 0.661 |
| 21-day | 20 | **−1.32%** | 50% | +0.33% | 54% | **−1.22** | −1.13 | 0.938 |
| 63-day | 20 | **−2.25%** | 30% | +1.06% | 55% | **−1.33** | −1.20 | 0.961 |

Read it carefully. The "buy defense on war news" reflex predicts a **reliable positive
excess**. Instead the basket's excess over SPY after these shocks is **negative at every
horizon** — about **−1.3%** over the trading month and **−2.3%** over the quarter — with a
win-rate at or **below** a coin flip (30% at 63 days). None of it clears significance (plain
*t* between −0.2 and −1.3; HAC *t* the same), and a random 20-date draw beats the shocks
**94–96%** of the time. The rally isn't merely unproven — in this sample the point estimate
points the **wrong way**: defense tends to *lag* the market in the weeks after a shock (the
move is largely priced on/before the headline, then a mild "sell-the-news" drift).

## The individual events — a wide, lottery-like spread

21-day excess-over-SPY per shock — a handful of big winners, as many big losers:

| shock | 21-day excess | shock | 21-day excess |
|---|--:|---|--:|
| 1998-08-20 (Sudan/Afghan strikes) | +2.54% | 2017-04-07 (Syria Tomahawks) | +2.60% |
| 1998-12-16 (Desert Fox) | **−12.92%** | 2018-04-13 (Syria strikes) | −8.03% |
| 1999-03-24 (Kosovo) | +0.14% | 2019-09-16 (Abqaiq) | −3.17% |
| 2001-09-17 (post-9/11) | +4.33% | 2020-01-03 (Soleimani) | −1.91% |
| 2001-10-08 (Afghanistan) | −8.52% | 2021-08-16 (Kabul falls) | −2.59% |
| 2003-03-20 (Iraq invasion) | −1.64% | 2022-02-24 (Ukraine) | **+6.24%** |
| 2008-08-08 (Georgia) | +3.11% | 2023-10-09 (post-Oct-7) | +3.04% |
| 2011-03-21 (Libya) | −3.98% | 2024-04-15 (Iran→Israel) | +0.44% |
| 2014-03-03 (Crimea) | −1.49% | 2024-10-01 (Iran barrage) | −6.87% |
| 2014-09-23 (ISIS strikes) | +1.14% | 2015-09-30 (Russia→Syria) | +1.06% |

The famous Ukraine-2022 and post-9/11 pops are real — but Desert Fox (−13%), the Afghanistan
invasion (−8.5%) and the 2024 Iran barrage (−6.9%) are just as large the other way. Twenty
draws this dispersed average to a small *negative* number you cannot distinguish from luck.

## Robustness — flat (and negative) across the window length

| window | n | cond. mean | plain *t* | HAC *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 20 | −0.14% | −0.19 | −0.19 | 0.661 |
| 10-day | 20 | −0.67% | −0.77 | −0.78 | 0.878 |
| 21-day | 20 | −1.32% | −1.22 | −1.13 | 0.938 |
| 42-day | 20 | −1.58% | −1.01 | −0.87 | 0.927 |
| 63-day | 20 | −2.25% | −1.33 | −1.20 | 0.961 |

There is no window at which the excess turns positive, let alone significant; the longer you
hold, the *more* defense lags. The sector ETF **ITA** (from 2006, 14 of the shocks) tells the
same story: 21-day excess **−0.87%**, win-rate **43%**, *t* = **−1.32**, placebo *p* = **0.86**.

## Costs barely matter — which is itself the point

| window | n trades | gross mean | net @ 10 bps round-trip |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 20 | −0.14% | −0.24% |
| 21-day | 20 | −1.32% | −1.42% |
| 63-day | 20 | −2.25% | −2.35% |

A 10-bps all-in round-trip on the long-basket / short-SPY pair shaves a tenth of a point off a
multi-week hold — costs are **not** the problem. There is **no positive edge to charge them
against**, and even a real one couldn't be a strategy: **20 trades in 31.5 years** (≈ one every
1.6 years) is not a NAV-scale rule.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, and small samples are weak

On a deterministic defense frame where the basket is `beta·SPY + idiosyncratic noise` (so the
excess has **zero** expected value by construction) with **20 shocks injected** and a SPY-like
market, the event study behaves exactly as it should:

| planted 21-day edge | detected | cond. mean | base mean | plain *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no edge) | 20 | +0.84% | −0.53% | **0.61** | 0.151 |
| **+6%/window** (huge edge) | 20 | +6.76% | −0.16% | **4.63** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted edge the test does **not** cross *t* = 2 (it cannot manufacture
significance from 20 events even when noise tilts the point estimate up). A **+6%/month**
planted edge — enormous — drives *t* to 4.6 and *p* to 0. The control proves two things at
once: the measurement engine is unbiased, **and** 20 events is too few to detect any edge of
plausible magnitude. (A synthetic control is a machinery proof, never market evidence.)

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The believers predict a reliable positive excess; the real tape delivers a
  **negative, insignificant** one at every horizon (21-day **−1.32%**, plain *t* = **−1.22**,
  HAC *t* = **−1.13**, placebo *p* = **0.94**), confirmed by the ITA ETF (*t* = −1.32). There is
  no shock-conditional defense edge — if anything a mild post-headline *lag*. Not REAL, not even
  WEAK: **NONE**.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no positive edge to deploy, costs are negligible (so they
  aren't the constraint), and **20 events in 31.5 years** could never be a NAV-scale strategy
  anyway. A market-neutral "buy defense on the headline" trade loses money gross and net.
- **Reliable rally? — BUSTED.** The "defense always pops on war news" reflex is a **vivid-event
  + base-rate illusion**: a couple of unforgettable rallies (Ukraine 2022, post-9/11) get
  generalised into a law, while the equally large losers (Desert Fox, the Afghanistan invasion,
  the 2024 Iran barrage) are forgotten. Averaged honestly over 20 shocks, defense does **not**
  beat the market — it slightly trails it.
